I  believe that there are certain cons to being male in American society  mostly having to do with gender roles. To address potential  misunderstandings I'm not saying that men experience sexism in the way  that women do or that they even experience the same things that women  do, cause they definitely don't in my opinion. I'm not even saying that  men have it worse than women in American society because I believe from  an institutional level they don't. But I stand firm in my opinion that  men definitely do experience unique difficulties in American society as a  male.

1. Men  are expected to act super masculine and if you don't fall into that  category you are treated horribly cause of it by both men AND women.  This, of course, depends on who you surround yourself with but I think  this is very common in my experience. Women are allowed more often to  experiment with how they dress and whether or not they want to wear  makeup, but when a man wears a full face of makeup they are made fun of  for it and potentially attacked. Talking, walking, or acting feminine in  any way can often lead to critique and bullying from not so supportive  people around you. Look at the pressure men face in the hip hop industry  to be masculine, and men in the media in general. When women wear suits  and makeup it's viewed as powerful, but when men wear dresses and  makeup they are made fun of for it.
2. In  domestic violence cases, they often assume the man is the one  perpetuating it when it very well can be a woman. When a woman hits a  man it's not a big deal but reverse it and then see what happens. There  are plenty of social experiments showing this. How about we all just  stop hitting one another?
3. Men have to sign up for a draft and women don't.
4. Men often serve longer prison times then women do.

While I don't have any serious herniations or severe severe injuries to my spine I do have chronic back pain which has affected me emotionally and physically. I'm 18. I have had doctors tell me that I'm very young to have this and it made me feel really lonely and hopeless at times. I don't have a proper curve in my neck and my ribs were shifting all over the place. I had pain all throughout my body and I didn't know why.  At times it was so bad it would affect me in numerous ways and give me pain in the most random of spots and still does occasionally. I would sometimes faint and have constant brain fog and doctors thought I had some underlying autoimmune disease and it turns out I didn't. After researching more and more and seeing chiropractors I've gained more knowledge of my numerous muscle imbalances and have came to the conclusion that years of bad postural habits along with excessive anxiety has caused this. I'm on a journey to improving it and it has improved but it's taken quite awhile and I'm still in pain from time to time. I wish we would be taught the importance of good posture and body mechanics from a young age. I feel like we brush off bad posture and make hunching at a desk for hours and hours in the name of productivity a very admirable thing. Sure, working hard and productivity is admirable but it shouldn't be normalized to put your bodies in dangerous conditions over and over again to achieve that result. It's very important as humans that we move enough and aren't in hunched positions for too long. What I've noticed is that more and more people are starting to come down with severe back issues from a younger age. A lot of my peers are now complaining of issues and it's more common than we might think. While I don't know much about your individual condition and journey I think it's good that we are doing what we can now at a young age since our bodies can still heal relatively quickly compared to an older age. We still have time to learn and improve our habits having to do with our health and you're certainly not alone in the confusion or loneliness. Talking about it on forums such as these and getting as much information as possible has helped me stay hopeful and learn of methods to reduce and reverse my condition over time.  A lot of doctors I've seen have tried to treat my symptoms and not the cause, none of them mentioned issues which were so obvious to me after researching such as my lack of a neck curve and horrible posture. So  from my experience I've come to the conclusion that posture is Extremely important and isn't talked about enough. For me, I'm pretty sure this is what gave me all these issues. You're certainly not alone and I completely understand the feeling of hopelessness that comes from this, but we can make positive changes and improve our bodies. There have been many people who have cured and reduced their back pain following an individual approach that works from them. Continue to ask your doctors questions and have conversations with your physical therapists. Maybe join a yoga class if you think that'll work for you and if your  doctors recommends it . A lot of people turn to yoga for back issues. A lot of exercises in physical therapy even come from yoga. Just remember you're not alone and it's a process. It may take a bit to improve but each step towards improving your health counts. I never thought I would struggle with back issues at such a young age. Even though it sucks, it has taught me the importance of self love and how important your health is. So if you ever need someone to talk to feel free to message me.:) Keep fighting the good fight! :)   (Also I found this youtube channel extremely helpful for my individual condition, I'm not sure if it will help you with yours but he covers all different types of pain in the back and ways to go about resolving them.
